svg.title: Threat model of a secure enclave
svg.desc: A hand-drawn systems sketch showing an untrusted main processor talking to an isolated secure enclave across a single narrow channel, a direct human presence channel with no return display path, an external state store, a manufacturing boundary crossed once, and a physical attack surface surrounding the whole system. Three weak points are marked: the hostile client channel, the missing trusted display path, and the unverifiable manufacturing root.

g.text: A coprocessor holds keys the main OS can request but never read. Three questions decide whether that promise holds.
Device secret: generated on die, or injected?
Fab, packaging, and test each handle the part
Factory test access fused off, unverified by whom

svg.text: Decap, probing, optical fault injection, EM, power and timing side channels.
Buys cost and needs physical possession. It does not scale.

g.text: Untrusted: runs the OS and every app
The only display the human has
Cannot be authenticated by the enclave
Whatever must stay correct so a key is both
unextractable and only usable on approved terms.
Own boot ROM and firmware: independent root of trust
Key store: policy is fixed per key at creation,
Crypto engine: constant time, fault monitored
Own memory, isolated from the main processor
1. Safe how: not extractable, or not usable?
2. Who is your client: the only caller is hostile
3. No screen: who tells the human what they approve?
Has no display of its own
Presence must be fresh and bound
to one operation, not a window

svg.text: Gold arrows are flows the enclave still governs even though its only caller is hostile.
Dashed red arrows mark where that control runs out.
1. Hostile client: the enclave's sole caller is the party you distrust.
2. No trusted display: the prompt is rendered by a liar.
3. Unverifiable root: attestation is circular, so you trust the manufacturer.
